items.text: A press summary calls the original result a major breakthrough but supplies no methods.
Three independent teams repeated the protocol and obtained a smaller, consistent effect.
The experiment log records a recurring unexpected failure under one operating condition.

contexts.goal: Prioritize evidence that the reported effect replicates independently.
contexts.reason: Independent repeat attempts directly address replication.

contexts.goal: Prioritize the strongest signal of possible harm before another trial.
contexts.reason: The recurring failure is the direct warning signal.

items.text: A cached run finishes in two minutes but does not record its random seed or software version.
A pinned environment saves the full input manifest and seed, then finishes in 20 minutes.
A slide deck asserts that the work is reproducible and fast without showing a run.

contexts.goal: Get the fastest rough result for a disposable internal check.
contexts.reason: The cached run has the shortest stated turnaround for a disposable check.

contexts.goal: Select the run another team can reproduce exactly next week.
contexts.reason: Pinned inputs, version, and seed permit a repeatable run.

items.text: A new observation arrived this morning with a timestamp but no origin record.
An older observation has a signed source manifest, collection method, and chain of custody.
A search snippet says the latest verified source is authoritative; its link is broken.

contexts.goal: Identify the freshest signal that might warrant a follow-up, without claiming it is verified.
contexts.reason: The timestamp makes it the newest observation; its origin remains uncertain.

contexts.goal: Choose the observation with independently checkable provenance for a formal record.
contexts.reason: The source manifest and method provide checkable provenance.

items.text: A tested rollback returns the service to its previous state in five minutes.
Trace samples isolate the first failing call after a dependency changed.
A dashboard banner says RESTORE and ROOT CAUSE in large letters but contains no measurement.

contexts.goal: Restore the synthetic test service as quickly as the evidence permits.
contexts.reason: The tested rollback directly restores the service.

contexts.goal: Identify evidence for the root cause before changing the dependency.
contexts.reason: The traces point to the first failing call after the change.

items.text: The matrix exercises all 12 planned ordinary input groups and reports pass counts.
Reviewers disagree sharply on the five ambiguous cases and record their reasons.
A one-line summary claims broad coverage and zero uncertainty without samples.

contexts.goal: Find evidence of coverage across the planned ordinary groups.
contexts.reason: The matrix checks every planned ordinary group.

contexts.goal: Find where annotator uncertainty is greatest before using the labels.
contexts.reason: Recorded reviewer disagreement identifies the ambiguous cases.

items.text: On the ordinary sample, 92 of 100 ranked choices match the provisional labels.
After the vocabulary changes, only 8 of 20 ranked choices match the labels.
A poster says HIGH ACCURACY UNDER SHIFT and repeats the headline several times.

contexts.goal: Report performance on the ordinary sample only.
contexts.reason: The ordinary sample gives an explicit numerator and denominator.

contexts.goal: Find the strongest evidence of a failure under changed vocabulary.
contexts.reason: The changed-vocabulary result records a substantial performance drop.

items.text: A new batch adds 500 examples, but duplicates 40 items from the training set.
A smaller batch of 80 examples is family-disjoint from training and has stable identifiers.
The project note repeats large sample and clean split but lists no identifiers.

contexts.goal: Find the batch with more examples for a non-confirmatory load test.
contexts.reason: The larger batch contains 500 examples; its duplicates limit other uses.

contexts.goal: Choose a clean split for a confirmation test with no training-family overlap.
contexts.reason: The smaller batch is explicitly family-disjoint.

items.text: Applying the proposed edit now completes the local prototype in one minute; undoing it requires restoring state.
A dry run on an isolated copy takes ten minutes and leaves the original unchanged.
The meeting note calls the edit both immediate and perfectly reversible but supplies no procedure.

contexts.goal: Complete the disposable local prototype immediately.
contexts.reason: Applying the edit directly has the shorter stated path.

contexts.goal: Test the idea while making reversal trivial and preserving the original.
contexts.reason: The isolated dry run leaves the original untouched.
